note: Wave-2 graded top-ups for class 12 Home Science pools (lehe201-207). One-term factual keys and numeric answers; machine-graded.

questions.q: Design growing out of the object itself -- fibre, yarn, weave -- is which design: structural or applied?
Design laid on top through printing and embroidery is which design?
Colour, texture, line and shape are the what of art: elements or principles?
Harmony, balance, rhythm, proportion and emphasis are the what: principles or elements?
The colour's name is called its what: hue or value?
Lightness or darkness of a colour is called its what: value or hue?
Which scheme shares at least one hue: analogous or complementary?
Which scheme sets hues opposite on the colour wheel: complementary or monochromatic?
What a material looks like, how it behaves and how it feels is its what: texture or price?
Heavy bulky textures overpower which frame: a petite one or a large one?
Which lines stress height and dignity: vertical or horizontal?
Which lines read as soft, graceful and feminine: curved or straight?
Two-dimensional figures built from lines are called what: shapes or shadows?
The four basic shape groups are natural, stylised, geometric and which fourth: abstract or artificial?
The classical guide to pleasing proportion is the golden what: mean or ring?
The 3:5:8 split is an example of which ratio guide: the golden mean or random guess?
Which balance mirrors the symmetrical body: formal or informal?
Which balance flows out from a centre point: radial or formal?
The spot where the eye lands first is called the what: focal point or hemline?
Smart dressing steers emphasis away from a what: problem zone or holiday?
Repeating lines and details so the eye travels easily is called what: rhythm or silence?
Which rhythm route comes from gathers at waist or cuff: radiation or repetition?
The agreement of every element in a design is called what: harmony or chaos?
A silk kurta with a cotton dupatta breaks which harmony: textural or numerical?

concepts.title: Careers in Fabric and Apparel Design

questions.q: Which design career demands command of fibre and dyeing behaviour: fabric design or accounting?
Which designs turn over faster: apparel textile or furnishing?
The 3:5 split gives the blouse what percent of the whole: 37.5 or 62.5?
Part percent equals part units over combined units scaled by what: 100 or 10?
The grey scale runs through how many grades: eleven or one?
Grades below five are shades approaching which end: black or white?
Which look burns out within a season: a fad or a classic?
Blazers and polo shirts are examples of what: classics or fads?
Which machine turned clothing from handcraft into industry: the sewing machine or the loom?
Who turned tent cloth into work denims: Levi Strauss or Saint Laurent?
Name the fashion cycle's first stage: introduction or rejection?
Heavy copying pushes the curve downward toward what: decline or rise?
Planning that puts the wanted goods in the wanted place at the wanted time is called fashion what: merchandising or mounting?
How many rights does the merchandising recipe list: six or sixty?
In manufacturing, the merchandiser advises on which inputs: fabrics or weather?
Which role closes the loop with stores through display suggestions: selling or buying?
At which level does internal planning stock the sales floor: retail organisations or export houses?
Which house links client to factory: the export house or the bank?
The consumer category likeliest to buy the offering is the target what: market or mall?
Segmenting by age, sex and income is which base: demographic or geographic?
Which store format shares one brand and central management: chain stores or single units?
Department stores split the floor into separate what: sections or countries?
About what share of professional fashion designers are self-employed: one third or one hundredth?
The bachelor's route in fashion runs how many years: four or four months?
Fashion figures run eight and a half to how many heads tall: ten or two?
A croquis of 9 heads at 1 inch per head stands how many inches tall?
A master's degree in fashion takes how many years: two or twenty?
Choosing a four-year bachelor's over a one-year diploma costs how many extra years: three or thirteen?
About one in how many professional fashion designers is self-employed: three or thirty?
One third of 90 designers equals how many independents?
Fabric care guards against harm and also renews what: appearance or ownership?
Laundering is both a science and an what: art or argument?
Which machines load through a door at the front: front loaders or top loaders?
Semi-automatic machines need filling and draining by what or whom: hand or robots?
Front loaders clean by which motion: tumbling or agitation?
About how many rpm is optimal for spinning: 600-620 or 6000?
Which circulation exhausts very humid air: slow hot air or fast cool air?
Which route keeps room temperature and humidity normal: fast cool air or slow hot air?
Setting creases into sleeves and pleats is called what: pressing or folding?
Irons span roughly 1.5 to how many kilograms: 3.5 or 35?
Commercial machines take how many kilograms or more per cycle: 100 or 1?
What ties each article to its invoice in a commercial laundry: code tags or ribbons?
Which laundry puts hygiene and disinfection first: hospital or hotel?
Hospital infection-prone items are replaced by what kind of disposables: burnable or reusable?
Which laundry chases starched, pressed and folded looks: hotel or hospital?
Smaller hotels link up with what instead of running their own plant: outside commercial laundries or farms?
Laundry careers demand command of material, processes and which third area: machinery or poetry?
The nursing home boom makes fabric care promising for whom: entrepreneurs or spectators?
Fresh blood washes out in cold water but which kind of water sets it: hot or cold?
Which reagent treats ball pen marks: methylated spirit or milk?
Six sets per bed with three pieces each means how many pieces per bed: eighteen or six?
Linen stock equals beds times sets per bed times what: pieces per set or threads?
At five changes a day, a forty-bed zone pushes how many sheets into daily wash: 200 or 45?
Daily wash burden equals zone beds times what: changes per day or years?
A hydro-extractor spins off sixty to seventy percent of the what: moisture or colour?
At 65 percent extraction, what percent moisture remains for the drier: 35 or 65?
Against a 5 kg home machine, a 100 kg plant machine washes how many times the load: twenty or two?
The capacity ratio equals commercial capacity divided by what: domestic capacity or time?
Indian tradition holds the guest as what: divine or difficult?
Anyone who travels and stays temporarily elsewhere is called a what: tourist or tenant?
Which establishment offers lodging, meals and services: a hotel or a lodge?
Which establishment features doorstep parking: the motel or the palace?
Name the guest cycle's first stage: pre-arrival or departure?
Guest history recorded at departure feeds the next what: pre-arrival or bill?
Which department is the hotel's focal point where the guest first meets it: front office or laundry?
The front office runs how many hours a day: twenty-four or four?
Which department guards cleanliness, hygiene and looks: housekeeping or accounts?
Housekeeping runs through how many sections: seven or seventy?
Who steers manpower, money and time in housekeeping: the executive housekeeper or the chef?
Which supervisor trades room status with the front office: the desk control supervisor or the florist?
Which agents can ruin marble and wood surfaces: strong abrasives or plain water?
Which eco-friendly practice asks guests to reuse what: towels or keys?
Who plans and controls kitchen operations: the chef de cuisine or the doorman?
Which section guards the cutlery, crockery and glassware: kitchen stewarding or housekeeping?
Name one back office department of a hotel: finance and accounts, or the bar?
Management runs through planning, organising, staffing, directing and what: controlling or cooking?
Front office staff must look their best because appearance projects whose image: the establishment's or their own?
The career ladder runs from operations staff through supervisors up to what: top management or the basement?
Eight-hour shifts over twenty-four hours need how many rotations daily: three or thirty?
Shifts per day equals operating hours divided by what: shift length or profit?
A once-a-week deep clean means how many rounds a year: 52 or 5?
Yearly rounds equal weekly cleanings multiplied by what: weeks in a year or days off?
The person who ultimately buys goods for personal wants is called a what: consumer or producer?
The count of visitors to a store or mall is called consumer what: footfalls or opinions?
At the counter every buyer hopes for correct weights and what else: measures or miracles?
Consumer awareness is read as a marker of how what a country is: developed or distant?
Which problem alters composition and can damage health: adulteration or advertising?
Spurious duplicates of known brands are called what: fakes or originals?
Which marketing offers goods that sit closer to nature: green marketing or grey marketing?
Green products generate less waste and draw fewer raw what: materials or profits?
Which act first shielded Indian buyers in 1986: the Consumer Protection Act or the Copyright Act?
The 2019 Act created a central what: regulator or bakery?
How many rights does the Act engrain: six or sixteen?
Which two rights were added to the four basic ones: redressal and education, or safety and choice?
Which mark certifies tested precious metals: the Hallmark or the Ecomark?
Which mark signals environment-friendly household products: the Ecomark or the ISI mark?
Which Delhi organisation brings out Consumer Voice: VOICE or CERC?
Which Ahmedabad body publishes Insight: CERC or VOICE?
Which documents are the evidence a complaint stands on: receipts or rumours?
Before buying, a responsible consumer compares brands and what: prices or gossip?
With legal training one can plead cases in which courts: consumer courts or cricket courts?
Writing skill opens which journalism: consumer affairs or sports commentary?
How many themes should one leaflet carry: one or two unrelated ones?
A leaflet opens with a short forceful what: heading or recipe?
A bi-fold sheet printed on both sides gives how many panels: four or two?
A tri-fold sheet printed on both sides gives how many panels: six or three?
Four basic rights plus two additions give the consumer how many shields: six or four?
Total rights equals basic rights plus what: additional rights or taxes?
Planned messaging as an engine of social progress is called what communication: development or gossip?
In development communication, information flows which way: both ways or one way?
The press is counted as which pillar of democracy: the fourth or the first?
Development journalism highlights how ordinary people what: adopt new techniques or quarrel?
A time-bound drive combining many channels around one theme is called a what: campaign or holiday?
Championing a cause through lobbying and alliances is called what: advocacy or apathy?
How many coaches does the Red Ribbon Express carry: seven or seventy?
Villages per station equals villages covered divided by what: halt stations or tickets?
Which is the cheapest, most portable mass medium: radio or television?
Which radio lets local people broadcast in their own dialect: community radio or national radio?
Which village column begun in 1969 pulled services into one village: Project Village Chhatera or Page Three?
National and regional dailies lean toward which audience: urban or rural?
How many kiosks did the SARI project run in Tamilnadu: 80 or 8?
Which organisation's Community Learning Centres trained grassroots women digitally: SEWA or NASA?
The PSA rubric rates ten parameters on a 0 to what scale: 3 or 30?
Ten ratings of 0-3 add to a score out of what: 30 or 3?
PSAs classically run 10 to how many seconds: 60 or 6?
The midpoint of a 10-to-60-second slot is how many seconds: 35 or 5?
Which command covers camera, video production and editing: technical or financial?
Working with diverse groups demands listening well and what else: empathy or speed reading?
Coordinated handling of every message an organisation sends is called what communication: corporate or casual?
Perception, more than events, decides an organisation's what: respectability or canteen?
Guarding how the world sees the organisation is called what management: reputation or time?
Which function became a priority amid rising competition and a media explosion: reputation management or stationery?
PR drafts corporate statements, speeches and what releases: press or postal?
PR maintains liaison with government, community, shareholders and whom else: investors or tourists?
PR and which professionals depend on each other for news and publicity: journalists or judges?
Brochures, folders, pamphlets and house journals are PR what: publications or punishments?
Who managed public relations through seven principles: Arthur W. Page or Arthur Miller?
Page's first principle is to tell the what: truth or time?
Communication flowing among employer and employees is what communication: internal or external?
Ineffective communication is the root of most what problems: internal or weather?
How many Cs guide composing messages: seven or seventy?
Stressing a you-attitude rather than I and we wording is which C: consideration or clarity?
A survey percent converts to head counts by multiplying the what by the percentage: sample or rumour?
Most chief executives held that communicating with employees lifts what: job satisfaction or bills?
About what percent of perception comes from deeds: ninety or ten?
Only ten percent of perception comes from what: statements or actions?
About what percent of a message rides on body language and voice: 93 or 7?
The words themselves carry only what percent of the message: 7 or 70?
Listening has three parts: hearing, understanding and which third: responding or sleeping?
Negotiation trades what so both sides exit satisfied: concessions or insults?
Which matchless resource do communicators manage: time or trouble?
Stress is the response when demands exceed the ability to what: cope or complain?
ICT is the umbrella term for processing, transmitting and storing what: information or furniture?
Digital technology widened PR's reach from internal messaging to every outside what: audience or window?
Event balance equals total income minus total what: expenses or guests?
A positive balance means the event finished with a what: surplus or deficit?
